headline: The RBI opened a dollar sale window for India's three state oil refiners and imposed a 20 percent rupee risk reserve on large FX derivative trades from today, its heaviest rupee defence since 2013, hours before September CPI that a Reuters poll puts at a 23 month high of 5.40 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,811.54, up 0.59 percent, the Nasdaq Composite at 27,366.17, up 0.64 percent, and the Dow at 51,654.95, up 0.83 percent, after President Trump said the United States would not strike Iran before the November 3 midterms, which pulled WTI down to a 91.85 dollar settlement and let the 10 year yield steady at 5.244 percent after touching 5.34 percent the prior week. Software and cybersecurity names led the bounce from Thursday's air pocket, with Snowflake up 7.42 percent, Palantir up 5.17 percent to a record close and CrowdStrike up 4.57 percent, and the Treasury market is shut today for Columbus Day before bank earnings on Tuesday and September CPI on Wednesday.
summary.india: The Nifty closed Friday at 22,520.45, up 1.30 percent, and Bank Nifty at 55,256.65, up 1.36 percent, snapping an eight week losing run that Business Today called the longest in 25 years, helped by a TCS September quarter profit of 13,884 crore rupees that beat the CNBC-TV18 poll and by crude easing. Foreign investors still sold a net 3,569 crore rupees on Friday against 4,743 crore rupees of domestic buying, the rupee finished at 96.73 against its May record low of 96.96, and the RBI responded over the weekend with a dollar window for Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL plus tighter FX derivative rules effective today.
summary.global: Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed Friday up 1.79 percent at 24,211.35 while the Nikkei 225 ended flat at 69,030.92 and Korea and Taiwan were shut, and in Europe the FTSE 100 added 1.06 percent to 10,552.05 and the DAX 1.13 percent to 25,087.27 on the same Iran headline. Korea has reopened weak, with the KOSPI down about 2.5 percent in early trade and Samsung Electronics off a similar amount on foreign selling despite a record quarterly profit forecast, while gold at 4,235 dollars, silver at 61.62 dollars and copper at 6.73 dollars a pound all firmed and bitcoin held near 83,700 dollars, still 27 percent below a year ago.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
